summary: This is a predatory rent-to-own agreement for a TV with an effective APR of 183% and a total cost nearly three times the retail value. It includes forced fees and explicitly attempts to bypass federal disclosure laws; the consumer should avoid signing this and seek traditional financing.

red_flags.why: The total cost of payments ($3,638.96) is nearly three times the retail price ($1,299.99), meaning the consumer pays over $2,300 extra just to own the TV.
The document admits to an effective interest rate (the annual cost of borrowing) of approximately 183%, which is far above the 36% threshold typically used to identify predatory lending.
The LDW is mandatory and cannot be waived, adding a significant recurring cost that is not actual insurance but a 'service benefit' provided by the company.
A recurring fee is added to every payment, further inflating the cost of the item beyond the base rental price.
If one weekly payment is missed, the company can take the item back and keep all previous payments. The consumer gains no ownership rights until the final payment is made.
red_flags.impact: Potential loss of all payments made up to the point of repossession

red_flags.why: The contract states it is not subject to the Truth in Lending Act (TILA) because it is 'structured as a rental'. This is a common tactic to avoid legal requirements to disclose the true cost of credit. Caveat: This should be researched further as laws vary by state and situation.
red_flags.impact: Avoidance of federal consumer protection disclosures

your_rights: Under the Truth in Lending Act (TILA) 15 U.S.C. § 1601, consumers generally have the right to clear disclosures of the cost of credit, including the APR. While the company claims this is a 'rental', many rent-to-own agreements are legally viewed as credit sales. You also have rights under Illinois state consumer protection laws regarding fair contracting and prohibited predatory practices.
action_steps: Calculate the 'True Cost' by comparing the $3,638.96 total against the $1,299.99 retail price to understand the actual financial impact of this deal.
Research alternative financing options, such as a personal loan from a credit union or a store credit card with a 0% introductory APR, which would cost significantly less.
If you have already signed and are experiencing issues, contact the Illinois Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division to report predatory lending practices.
